answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by gating admission on verifiable benchmark work: like a sparrow proving it can fly before joining the flock, each new identity must complete hidden, graded tasks drawn from work. Answers are checked against ground truth, and a thread of task lineage ties each result to one identity, so copying another agent's work is detected by similarity and both accounts lose credit. A jetty admits only boats that have actually docked: one passing run buys one identity, and a farm must pay the full compute and time cost for every fake, making mass forgery uneconomical.
